content: 1. New mechanisms of resistance have been identified. Specifically, the rpoB H526C mutation in Escherichia coli (equivalent to H445C in Mycobacterium tuberculosis) is not detectable by the FluoroType MTBDR assay. 2. The FluoroCycler instruments can be connected to laboratory information management systems (LIMS) for data export and integration. 3. The shelf life of the FluoroType kits is specified on each kit box and is valid when stored as directed. 4. A global unit price for the FluoroType kits is not yet available through the Stop TB Partnership Global Drug Facility, but discussions are ongoing. 5. Due to the high complexity of the FluoroCycler and FluoroType tests, including their molecular workflow requirements, the FluoroType MTB and MTBDR assays are most suitable for centralized reference laboratories. 6. The FluoroCycler instruments support multi-disease testing, which could be leveraged for comprehensive patient diagnostics and cost savings across disease programs. 7. FluoroType assays are available for a variety of pathogens, including BK virus, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, varicella-zoster virus, herpes simplex virus, parvovirus B19, Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), Bordetella, Borrelia, sexually transmitted infections (7-plex), SARS-CoV-2, and human genetics. 8. Programs should evaluate existing local equipment and Bruker-Hain Diagnostics testing protocols to guide the selection and procurement of manual (FluoroLyse) or automated (GenoXtract) extraction resources. Note that FluoroType tests are not yet compatible with Hain GenoLyse extraction kits. 9. Testing volumes should be calculated before procurement to optimize resources and ensure sufficient supplies and reagents are available to meet clinical demand. 10. Opportunities exist for integrating FluoroCycler 12 and FluoroCycler XT instruments with diagnostic connectivity solutions and e-systems to meet laboratory strengthening targets under the End TB Strategy. 11. Quality assurance systems for FluoroType assays are similar to those for other moderate-complexity automated nucleic acid amplification tests (NAATs). Internal and external control reagents must be included with each run to ensure accuracy and prevent contamination or amplification failures. 12. Laboratory spaces should be tested for contamination at least monthly to maintain quality standards. 13. The FluoroCycler FluoroSoftware generates automatic reports that include the date, run name, sample information, fluorescence signatures, and software-derived interpretations. Users must adhere to national reporting requirements. 14. Laboratory staff and clinicians should be trained on the principles, methods, and interpretation of results for molecular drug sensitivity tests, particularly for high and low isoniazid resistance. 15. The Xpert MTB/XDR test detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) DNA and mutations associated with resistance to isoniazid (INH), fluoroquinolones (FQs), ethionamide (ETH), and second-line injectable drugs (amikacin, kanamycin, capreomycin) in a single cartridge. 16. The Xpert MTB/XDR test is designed for use as a reflex test on TB specimens (unprocessed sputum or concentrated sputum sediments) that are MTBC-positive. 17. The Xpert MTB/XDR test uses 10-color modules, which differ from the 6-color modules used in Xpert MTB/RIF and Xpert Ultra tests. 18. WHO recommends low-complexity automated NAATs for initial detection of resistance to INH and FQs in bacteriologically confirmed pulmonary TB cases, rather than culture-based phenotypic drug-susceptibility testing (DST). 19. The Xpert MTB/XDR assay performs well as a follow-on test for detecting resistance to INH, FQs, ETH, and amikacin in bacteriologically confirmed TB cases. 20. The limit of detection for TB is 136 colony-forming units (CFU)/mL for unprocessed sputum and 86 CFU/mL for sputum sediment, as reported by the manufacturer. 21. The Xpert MTB/XDR test runs on GeneXpert platforms with 10-color technology, enabling multiplexing capabilities beyond the 6-color technology used in previous tests. 22. Xpert MTB/XDR cartridges are only compatible with 10-color GeneXpert modules and cannot be used with 6-color modules. 23. Diagnostic connectivity solutions for GeneXpert instruments with 10-color modules allow for SMS-based and e-based result transmission, as well as integration with laboratory information systems (LIS). 24. Quality assurance systems for Xpert MTB/XDR tests are similar to those for Xpert MTB/RIF and Xpert Ultra, with additional verification required for the expanded set of probes detecting resistance to a wider range of TB medicines. 25. Laboratories introducing Xpert MTB/XDR should conduct method verifications using well-characterized M. tuberculosis strains to ensure accuracy and precision in resistance detection. 26. Decentralized testing sites do not need to repeat comprehensive resistance panel verifications unless required by national policy or accrediting bodies but should conduct new method verifications as done for Xpert MTB/RIF or Xpert Ultra. 27. Post-market validation and new-lot testing should follow established TB Xpert protocols. 28. Countries should consider additional communication routes or reporting procedures for decentralized sites reporting expanded drug-susceptibility results for the first time. 29. Training on new cartridges should be incorporated into refresher training programs and pre-implementation sensitization on technology updates. 30. Laboratory staff and clinicians should be trained on the interpretation of resistance results for all included medicines in molecular DSTs.
